text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam wishes to restore and develop relations with traditional friends like the Czech Republic.
-- Vietnam is prepared to go it alone in building the nation's first oil refinery at Dung Quat on the central coast.
-- Overseas Vietnamese are being encouraged to invest in the fields of science and technology.
-- The government has reaffirmed its determination to push ahead with an oil refinery at Dung Quat on the central coast even though the location is seen as controversial.
-- Australia and Vietnam have agreed to speed up cooperation in infrastructure, mining, agriculture and food processing despite temporary financial difficulties on Canberra's side.
-- Vietnam reported crude oil output of 1.2 million tonnes in the first 45 days of 1997.
-- Nine people were killed in an accident when a boat sank in Quang Ninh province earlier this week.
-- Australian Prime Minister John Howard has accepted an invitation from Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet to visit Vietnam.
-- Vietnam sold 10 billion dong ($893,734) of one-year treasury notes with an annual of 10.99 percent to Vietnam's Bank for Foreign Trade in an auction on Wednesday.
-- The Speaker of the Russian State will pay an official friendship visit to Vietnam at the invitation of National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh.
-- Construction of a $650 million hydropower station in the coastal province of Binh Thuan started on Tuesday.
